solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The PM is perturbed about a fellow on board

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the A
perturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister is flustered about some person on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perturbed' shuffles THEPMIS into SHIPMTE, and 'about' wraps those letters around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipmate is a fellow sailor or passenger travelling on the same vessel.

clue.text: Principal policy that gets first reading?

parts.note: the principal of a school is its head
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A headteacher's policy that is read out first.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: a newspaper reader reads this before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A headline is the large title at the top of a newspaper story, the part readers see before the article.

clue.text: Coward's acts soldier survives

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier
lives means survives

explanation.surface: A cowardly deed lets a soldier come through alive.
explanation.walkthrough: Coward is not a timid person but Noël Coward, the English playwright; 'acts' are the divisions of his play.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Lives is a 1930 comedy in three acts by the playwright Noël Coward.

clue.text: Unfortunately, a couple from Kansas are in detached state

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of regret, meaning unfortunately
the first two letters of Kansas

explanation.surface: Sadly, two Kansans are stuck in a remote, aloof condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detached' means separate from the rest: this US state does not border the other mainland states.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is a US state cut off from the contiguous forty-eight by Canada.

clue.text: Part of area's tourist quarter put right on the map

definitions.text: quarter put right on the map

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the district's visitor area is marked on the right of a map.
explanation.definitionFit: On a conventional map north is at the top, so the eastern compass point sits at the right.

clue.text: Removal of most locks, as a way to save time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a haircut taking off most of the hair

explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests doors or canals, but they are locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a cropped hairstyle and a quicker route or method.

clue.text: A certain amount of mass attack's ending, as heard on radio

definitions.meaning: first meaning: short for kilogram, a unit of mass

definitions.text: attack's ending, as heard on radio
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the last letter of attack is K, which radio operators call by this code word

explanation.walkthrough: The NATO phonetic alphabet used in radio speech gives each letter a code word, and that for K is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilo is a thousand grams, and in the radio spelling alphabet it stands for the letter K.

clue.text: Maintain watch on second escort

parts.note: to take someone out is to escort them on a date

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye on a second date.
explanation.definitionFit: Police stake out a place when they keep it under covert surveillance.

clue.text: I put in short pieces on a page

definitions.text: I put in short pieces on a page

indicators.note: on puts the jumbled part after A and P
put in means the I is inserted into the jumbled letters
short in pieces means the word short is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer explains that they place brief sayings on each sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' breaks SHORT into HORST, and 'put in' sets I inside to make HORIST, which follows A and P. Read whole, the clue is what such a writer says.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphorist composes aphorisms, pithy sayings that state a truth in few words.

clue.text: After misdirected youth, one becomes artist

indicators.note: After places the I behind the rearranged letters
misdirected means sent the wrong way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a youth is a lad
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A wayward young man reforms and turns into a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misdirected' scrambles the youth, a lad, and one is the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was the Spanish surrealist painter.

clue.text: Work in house no resident contributes to

definitions.text: Work in house no resident contributes to

parts.words: Work in house no resident contributes to
parts.note: a book kept in a house or stately home which guests, not those who live there, sign and write comments in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' suggests labour, but it is a written work: a book that only guests write in.
explanation.definitionFit: Stately homes and hotels keep a ledger for callers to sign and leave remarks, never the occupants.

clue.text: Courses carefully weighed in hung parliament?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: meals planned to give the right mix of nutrients
second meaning, cryptically: a diet is a parliament (as in Japan's), and a hung one is evenly balanced

explanation.walkthrough: A hung parliament has no majority; a Diet is the name of some national assemblies.
explanation.definitionFit: A healthy eating plan has its food groups in proper proportion, like a legislature split evenly.

clue.text: Divert first of two vehicles I had turned round

indicators.note: turned round means the whole string is read backwards
first of picks the opening letter of the word two

parts.note: its first letter is T
carts are vehicles
I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone distracts attention by spinning two of their vehicles round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned round' acts on all three pieces together, not just 'I had' beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To distract someone is to divert their attention elsewhere.

clue.text: A club that can win if player's heartless, say? Blast!

definitions.text: A club that can win if player's heartless, say
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a card of the ... suit, such as a club, wins a trick when the player has no hearts left to follow

explanation.walkthrough: In whist or bridge a player void in the suit led may play a card of the trump suit and win; 'heartless' means out of hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a card of the winning suit and, as a noun, the sound of a trumpet.

clue.text: Material from India, originally, incorporated by musical icon

indicators.note: incorporated by says the answer is held within the following words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of musical into icon

explanation.surface: A star of the musical stage takes on some Indian fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' belongs to the definition: calico takes its name from Calicut in India, where the cloth first came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain cotton cloth named after Calicut, the Indian port that first exported it.

clue.text: Close main line

parts.note: the main is an old word for the sea

explanation.surface: Reads like an instruction to shut off a principal pipe or railway route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like an adjective but is the poetic noun for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To seal something is to close it up so nothing gets in or out.

clue.text: Something extra for consumer — channel on alternative to cable

indicators.note: on places one piece on top of, so before, the other in a down answer

parts.note: side was British slang for a television channel, as in 'the other side'
a satellite dish is the alternative to cable television

explanation.surface: A TV viewer chooses an extra channel on satellite rather than cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumer' suggests a shopper, but it is someone eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A side dish is an extra plate of food served beside the main course for the diner.

clue.text: Criticize inadequate service

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to find ... with, verb
second meaning: in tennis, a serve that lands out or in the net

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests complaining about poor treatment in a shop; the second sense is from tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for blaming and a tennis term for a serve that is not good.

clue.text: With source of needles, sedate as emergency treatment

parts.note: a fir tree is a source of pine needles
sedate and staid both mean calm and dignified

explanation.surface: A medic sedates a patient with drugs from needles in an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needles' and 'sedate' evoke injections; they are a conifer's needles and an adjective meaning sober.
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the immediate help given to an injured person before professional care arrives.

clue.text: Cold-blooded creature changed temperature

parts.note: something changed is new

explanation.surface: A reptile or amphibian whose body heat shifts with its surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed temperature' reads as the creature's behaviour, but it is two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt is an amphibian, and amphibians are ectothermic, relying on outside warmth.

clue.text: Exhibitionist's call to new security personnel

parts.note: a show-off cries 'watch me'

explanation.surface: A show-off calls out to newly hired guards.
explanation.definitionFit: Watchmen are guards employed to patrol and protect property.

clue.text: Don, for example, follows his lead in club

indicators.note: follows puts the river after the D

parts.note: his refers back to Don, and Don's first letter is D
the Don is a river, in Yorkshire and in Russia

explanation.surface: A man called Don trails behind his leader in a society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a man's name but is the river; 'club' is a golf club rather than a society.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is the golf club with a large head used for long shots off the tee.

clue.text: Functions to promote business in bars

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the work of promoting a business
functions are social events

explanation.surface: Corporate parties held in pubs to drum up trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like pubs, but it is a verb meaning blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to stop it happening, so bars and the answer both mean stops.

clue.text: Anger raised about team's performance-enhancing medication

indicators.note: about means going round, so the anger word surrounds the team
raised means lifted up, so in a down answer the letters are read upwards

parts.note: to rile is to anger
a team is an eleven, XI; lifted up with the rest in this down light it reads IX

explanation.surface: Fury rises over a team's use of drugs to boost results.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter means 'raised' to lift the whole of RILE-around-XI; lifting the anger word alone and setting the upturned eleven inside it comes to the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a potion supposed to restore vigour or prolong life, a magical tonic.

clue.text: Is fed, it's said, badly — hence this?

definitions.text: Is fed, it's said, badly — hence this?

indicators.note: badly means poorly arranged, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A diner fed poorly, so the story goes, is left unhappy as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: rearranging ISFEDITSSAID gives the answer, and being badly fed would leave you feeling that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fed badly leaves a person discontented, unhappy with what they received.

clue.text: Act as informer in either part of US prison

definitions.meaning: first meaning: criminal slang for giving information to the police
second meaning: a famous New York State jail has a doubled name, and each half is this word

explanation.walkthrough: The jail is Sing Sing, in New York State; its name is one word said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang, to confess or grass on accomplices is described with this verb.

clue.text: Game with call deciding winner at match point

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a children's card game

definitions.text: call deciding winner at match point
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the cry made when two matching cards appear

explanation.walkthrough: 'match point' sounds like tennis, but it is the moment two cards match.
explanation.definitionFit: In the card game of that name, the first to shout it when two identical cards show takes the pile.

clue.text: Bit of poetry from William Blake

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the poet's name that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of William into Blake

explanation.surface: A fragment of verse by the English Romantic poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Blake was a poet, so 'from William Blake' looks like an attribution, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of an unstressed then a stressed syllable, a unit of verse.

clue.text: Clad in silk, playing a piece of music

indicators.note: clad in means dressed in, so the word for playing is wrapped in the fabric

parts.note: satin is a glossy silk fabric
something playing is on

explanation.surface: A performer wearing silk plays a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clad in silk' describes 'playing', which wears the fabric: ON goes inside it, giving SONATIN before A.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonatina is a short or simple sonata, a composition for one or two instruments.

clue.text: Religious sailor's evil acts at sea

parts.note: pi is informal British for pious or religious
a rating is a non-commissioned sailor in the navy

explanation.surface: A devout seaman's misdeeds on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a British colloquialism; a rating is an ordinary sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy is robbery and violence committed on the high seas.
